newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish court rejects new law liberalising abortion.
newsitem.headline: Polish court rejects new law liberalising abortion.

text.p: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal ruled on Wednesday that a law passed last year, effectively allowing abortion on demand, clashes with the constitution and must be reexamined by parliament, tribunal officials said.
The tribunal ruling will encourage Pope John Paul, about to visit Poland on a May 31-June 10 pilgrimage, who was appalled by the liberalisation of abortion in his native country.

The issue divided Polish society last year and since President Aleksander Kwasniewski signed the liberalisation in November, pro-Catholic parties and the Church have been campaigning to have the law tightened again.

Among the court's objections was a lack of clear criteria applying to a clause in last year's amendment which allows women to terminate a pregnancy, until the 12th week, if they have difficult living conditions or other personal problems.

"Here there is a lack of clearly-defined criteria of what these difficult conditions mean and this was recognised as in conflict with the constitution," an official in the tribunal president's office told Reuters, adding he did not have full details as the decision was still being read out.

The new abortion law, already in force, now returns to parliament for re-examination. To overturn the court decision would require a two-thirds majority in parliament. Pending a decision the existing liberalised provisions continue to apply.

The issue has become a major theme in campaigning for parliamentary elections due around September, when pro-Catholic rightist parties grouped around the Solidarity trade union hope to supplant the secular-minded ex-communists now in government.
